title: 22nd Sitting of third session of 2025

items.text: Opening recitation (Hamd and Salawat); the sitting begins.
Roll call of members present at the sitting.
Announcement of the day's agenda (Agenda No. އޖ/22/3/2025).
Approval of the minutes of three previous sittings (minutes Nos. 15/3/2025 to 17/3/2025).

Written-answer question by Kendhoo MP Mauroof Zakir to Minister of Education Dr Ismail Shafeeu: why has work on the multi-purpose hall of B. Fulhadhoo School stopped, and when will it resume and be completed.

Written-answer question by Galolhu North MP Mohamed Ibrahim to Minister of Tourism and Environment Thoriq Ibrahim: if the ministry applies standards that treat regions differently when setting the acquisition cost of islands and lagoons, what are those differences.

Written-answer question by Galolhu North MP Mohamed Ibrahim to Minister of Tourism and Environment Thoriq Ibrahim: when will work to relocate the B. Goidhoo powerhouse from its current site begin, and when will it be completed.
Preliminary debate on the bill submitted by Galolhu South MP Meekail Ahmed Naseem to repeal Law No. 1/2013 (Freedom of Peaceful Assembly Act).
Preliminary debate on the bill to amend the Constitution of the Republic of Maldives, submitted on behalf of the government by Baarah MP Ibrahim Shujau.
Preliminary debate on the bill to amend Law No. 7/2010 (Decentralisation Act), submitted on behalf of the government by Inguraidhoo MP Ibrahim Falah.
Preliminary debate on the bill to amend Law No. 10/2010 (Local Council Elections Act), submitted on behalf of the government by Fuvahmulah North MP Hamad Abdulla.
Foreign Relations Committee report on the President's nomination for non-resident Ambassador of the Maldives to Antigua and Barbuda.
Social Committee report on the Animal Husbandry and Animal Welfare Bill.
Voting on items from the day's business that have reached the voting stage.

summary: The sitting approved old minutes, tabled written questions to the Education and Tourism ministers, opened debate on repealing the Peaceful Assembly Act and on constitutional, Decentralisation and Local Council Elections amendments, and took up reports on an ambassador nominee and the Animal Welfare Bill.
